title: ACCA TX - Taxation (UK)
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the ACCA TX (UK) syllabus study guide. Not a capture of past exam questions. Tax rules referenced are the principles in the syllabus, not current-year rates.

items.domain: The UK Tax System and Administration
items.stem: A new nationwide tax is proposed for the whole of the United Kingdom. Which source of UK tax law would formally impose this tax?
options: A decision of a local council
A press release issued by HMRC
items.explanation: UK taxes must be imposed by statute, so an Act of Parliament is the source of a new tax. Local councils, HMRC press releases and practice notes do not create or impose new taxes.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - The UK Tax System and Administration

items.domain: The UK Tax System and Administration
items.stem: An individual must file a self-assessment tax return online for a tax year. By what date must the return normally be submitted to avoid a late-filing penalty?
options: 31 October following the end of the tax year
31 January following the end of the tax year
5 April following the end of the tax year
31 July following the end of the tax year
items.explanation: The online self-assessment filing deadline is 31 January following the end of the tax year. Paper returns are due earlier, by 31 October, but this individual files online.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - The UK Tax System and Administration

items.domain: The UK Tax System and Administration
items.stem: HMRC wishes to enquire into an individual's self-assessment return that gives no indication of deliberate error. Within what period may HMRC normally issue the notice of enquiry?
options: Three months from the filing date
Six months from the end of the tax year
Twelve months from the filing date
Twenty-four months from the end of the tax year
items.explanation: For a return not involving deliberate error HMRC may normally open an enquiry within twelve months of the filing date. Longer periods apply only where deliberate understatement is suspected.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - The UK Tax System and Administration

items.domain: The UK Tax System and Administration
items.stem: An individual's income tax liability is large because almost all of her income is untaxed at source. When are her payments on account normally due?
options: 5 April and 5 October following the tax year
30 June and 31 December following the tax year
1 January and 1 July in the tax year
31 January in the tax year and 31 July following it
items.explanation: Payments on account are due in two equal instalments on 31 January in the tax year and 31 July following the end of the tax year. A balancing payment is then due on the following 31 January.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - The UK Tax System and Administration

items.domain: The UK Tax System and Administration
items.stem: An employee completes a self-assessment return reporting only employment income. For how long must she normally keep the records that support the return after the 31 January filing deadline?
items.explanation: An employee must normally keep supporting records for twelve months after the 31 January filing deadline. A longer five-year period applies to the records of a trade or business.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - The UK Tax System and Administration

items.domain: The UK Tax System and Administration
items.stem: A taxpayer deliberately conceals income in order to reduce his tax liability. On what basis does HMRC normally charge a penalty for this behaviour?
options: A fixed penalty unrelated to the tax at stake
A percentage of the tax understated, higher for deliberate concealment
A penalty equal to the tax correctly due
No penalty, because the return was submitted on time
items.explanation: Penalties for incorrect returns are expressed as a percentage of the potential lost revenue and increase with the taxpayer's behaviour, being highest for deliberate concealment. A fixed penalty does not reflect the tax avoided.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - The UK Tax System and Administration

items.domain: The UK Tax System and Administration
items.stem: A taxpayer disagrees with an HMRC assessment and wishes to appeal against it. To which body is the appeal normally made first?
items.explanation: Disputes about tax assessments are heard first by the First-tier Tribunal (Tax Chamber). The High Court, Court of Appeal and Supreme Court are higher courts reached only on further appeal.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - The UK Tax System and Administration

items.domain: The UK Tax System and Administration
items.stem: A tax avoidance arrangement has no commercial substance and its main purpose is to obtain a tax advantage. Which power does the General Anti-Abuse Rule give HMRC?
options: To refer the matter directly to the Supreme Court
To ignore the transaction and take no action
To impose a criminal conviction automatically
To counteract the tax advantage that arises
items.explanation: The General Anti-Abuse Rule allows HMRC to counteract the tax advantage arising from abusive arrangements that lack commercial substance. It does not by itself create a criminal offence or bypass the normal appeal route.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - The UK Tax System and Administration

items.stem: An employee earns a salary of 40,000 pounds and a bonus of 5,000 pounds. She pays 3,000 pounds into an occupational pension scheme under net pay arrangements. What is her taxable employment income before any personal allowance?
items.explanation: Total pay is 45,000 pounds. A net pay pension contribution is deducted from pay before tax, so the taxable figure is 45,000 pounds less 3,000 pounds, which is 42,000 pounds.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Income Tax and National Insurance

items.stem: An individual has adjusted net income of 110,000 pounds. Assuming a personal allowance of 12,570 pounds that is reduced by one pound for every two pounds of income above 100,000 pounds, what is her personal allowance?
items.explanation: Income above 100,000 pounds is 10,000 pounds, so the allowance falls by 10,000 pounds divided by two, or 5,000 pounds. Subtracting 5,000 pounds from 12,570 pounds leaves 7,570 pounds.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Income Tax and National Insurance

items.stem: A basic rate taxpayer receives 1,000 pounds of bank interest during the tax year. Assuming the personal savings allowance for a basic rate taxpayer is 1,000 pounds, how much of this interest is charged to income tax?
items.explanation: The personal savings allowance of 1,000 pounds covers the whole 1,000 pounds of interest for a basic rate taxpayer, so none of it is taxed. The allowance is lower for higher rate and additional rate taxpayers.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Income Tax and National Insurance

items.stem: An individual receives 2,000 pounds of dividend income and is a basic rate taxpayer. Assuming the dividend nil rate band is 1,000 pounds, how much dividend income is charged at the dividend basic rate?
items.explanation: The first 1,000 pounds of dividends is covered by the dividend nil rate band. The remaining 1,000 pounds is taxed at the dividend basic rate.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Income Tax and National Insurance

items.stem: A sole trader's delivery driver receives a parking fine while making a business delivery and the trader pays it. Is the fine an allowable trading deduction?
options: No, because fines for breaking the law are not deductible
No, unless the driver is self-employed
Yes, because it arose from a business journey
Yes, because it is a legal obligation of the business
items.explanation: Fines incurred for breaking the law are not wholly and exclusively for the purposes of the trade and are not allowable deductions. The purpose of the journey does not change this.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Income Tax and National Insurance

items.stem: A sole trader buys new machinery for 10,000 pounds and wants to claim the maximum allowance in the year of purchase. Assuming the annual investment allowance is 1,000,000 pounds, how much can she claim?
items.explanation: The annual investment allowance gives 100 percent relief on qualifying plant and machinery up to the allowance limit, so the full 10,000 pounds is deductible in the year of purchase.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Income Tax and National Insurance

items.stem: An individual lets a furnished room in her only home for 6,000 pounds during the tax year. Assuming rent-a-room relief of 7,500 pounds is available, how much of the rental income is taxable?
items.explanation: Because gross rents of 6,000 pounds are below the 7,500 pound rent-a-room limit, the rental profit is exempt and no tax is due. The exemption applies automatically unless the taxpayer elects otherwise.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Income Tax and National Insurance

items.stem: A landlord replaces a worn-out washing machine in a furnished let with a new one costing 500 pounds, receiving nothing for the old machine. Under replacement of domestic items relief, what deduction is available?
options: 0 pounds, because it is capital expenditure
500 pounds, being the net replacement cost
items.explanation: Replacement of domestic items relief allows a deduction for the net cost of replacing a domestic item, so with no disposal proceeds the full 500 pounds is deductible. The original purchase is not deductible, only the replacement.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Income Tax and National Insurance

items.stem: An employer provides an employee with a company car that is available for private use throughout the year. On what basis is the taxable benefit normally calculated?
options: A percentage of the car's list price based on its CO2 emissions
The actual running costs paid by the employer only
The fall in the car's market value during the year
A fixed amount set by HMRC each year
items.explanation: The company car benefit is the car's list price multiplied by a percentage that rises with the car's CO2 emissions. The employer's running costs and depreciation are not the basis of the calculation.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Income Tax and National Insurance

items.stem: An employer lends an employee 20,000 pounds interest-free for the whole tax year. Assuming the official rate of interest is 2.25 percent and the beneficial loan threshold is 10,000 pounds, what is the taxable benefit?
items.explanation: The benefit is the loan of 20,000 pounds multiplied by the official rate of 2.25 percent, giving 450 pounds. The threshold only removes small loans from the charge and does not exempt this one.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Income Tax and National Insurance

items.stem: An individual pays 8,000 pounds into a personal pension scheme under relief at source. Assuming basic rate income tax is 20 percent, what gross amount is credited to the pension fund?
items.explanation: Under relief at source the provider adds basic rate tax to the net payment. The net 8,000 pounds represents 80 percent of the gross, so the gross amount is 8,000 pounds divided by 0.8, which is 10,000 pounds.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Income Tax and National Insurance

items.stem: An employee's earnings are above the primary threshold and she therefore pays National Insurance on those earnings. Which class of contributions does she pay?
items.explanation: Employees pay Class 1 primary contributions through PAYE. Class 2 and Class 4 are paid by the self-employed, and Class 3 is voluntary.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Income Tax and National Insurance

items.stem: A self-employed sole trader has profits above the small profits threshold for the tax year. Which classes of National Insurance does she normally pay?
items.explanation: The self-employed pay Class 2 flat-rate contributions and Class 4 contributions based on profits. Class 1 is paid by employees and Class 3 is voluntary.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Income Tax and National Insurance

items.stem: An individual has gaps in his National Insurance record and wants to make voluntary contributions to improve his State Pension entitlement. Which class of contributions should he pay?
items.explanation: Class 3 contributions are voluntary contributions paid to fill gaps in a National Insurance record. Class 1 and Class 4 are compulsory on earnings or profits, and Class 2 is for the self-employed.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Income Tax and National Insurance

items.stem: A redundant employee receives a termination payment of 45,000 pounds that is not for contractual notice. Assuming the 30,000 pound exemption is available, what amount of the payment is taxable?
items.explanation: The first 30,000 pounds of a qualifying termination payment is exempt, so the taxable amount is 45,000 pounds less 30,000 pounds, which is 15,000 pounds. A payment for contractual notice would not qualify for the exemption.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Income Tax and National Insurance

items.stem: A higher rate taxpayer makes a Gift Aid donation of 400 pounds net to a registered charity. Assuming basic rate tax is 20 percent and higher rate tax is 40 percent, what additional relief can she claim?
items.explanation: The gross donation is 400 pounds divided by 0.8, which is 500 pounds. The difference between the higher rate of 40 percent and the basic rate of 20 percent applied to 500 pounds gives an additional 100 pounds of relief.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Income Tax and National Insurance

items.stem: An individual sells listed shares for 30,000 pounds that cost 18,000 pounds, incurring 500 pounds of incidental selling costs. What is the chargeable gain before the annual exempt amount?
items.explanation: The gain is proceeds of 30,000 pounds less the cost of 18,000 pounds and the incidental selling costs of 500 pounds, giving 11,500 pounds. Incidental costs of disposal are deductible in computing the gain.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Chargeable Gains

items.stem: An individual has chargeable gains of 5,000 pounds and allowable losses of 1,000 pounds in the tax year. Assuming the annual exempt amount is 3,000 pounds, what is the taxable gain?
items.explanation: Losses are set against gains first, leaving 4,000 pounds, and the annual exempt amount of 3,000 pounds is then deducted to give a taxable gain of 1,000 pounds. The exemption is applied after losses.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Chargeable Gains

items.stem: An individual sells an antique vase, a chattel, for 8,000 pounds that cost 3,000 pounds. Using the chattel marginal relief rule, what is the chargeable gain?
items.explanation: For proceeds between 6,000 and 15,000 pounds the gain is the lower of the actual gain of 5,000 pounds and five-thirds of the excess over 6,000 pounds, which is 3,333 pounds. Marginal relief therefore reduces the gain to 3,333 pounds.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Chargeable Gains

items.stem: An individual sells the only home she has owned and occupied as her main residence throughout ten years of ownership. How is the resulting gain treated for capital gains tax?
options: Taxable in full with no relief
Taxable on the last nine months only
Exempt only if she buys a replacement home
Fully exempt under principal private residence relief
items.explanation: Principal private residence relief exempts a gain on a dwelling that has been the taxpayer's main residence throughout the period of ownership. No replacement purchase is required for the exemption to apply.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Chargeable Gains

items.stem: An individual makes a 2,000,000 pound gain on shares that qualify for business asset disposal relief. Assuming the relief taxes the first 1,000,000 pounds of qualifying gains at 10 percent, what is the capital gains tax on that first 1,000,000 pounds?
items.explanation: Business asset disposal relief applies a 10 percent rate to the first 1,000,000 pounds of qualifying gains, giving tax of 100,000 pounds. The remaining gain is charged at the normal rate and is not part of this relief.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Chargeable Gains

items.stem: An individual sells shares and then buys the same class of shares in the same company within 30 days of the disposal. Which share identification rule applies to the disposal?
options: The disposal is exempt because shares were repurchased
The disposal is matched with the shares bought within the 30-day period
The disposal is matched only with shares held at the start
The disposal is matched with the most recent purchase regardless of date
items.explanation: Under the 30-day rule, shares disposed of are matched first with any shares of the same class acquired within the following 30 days. This prevents the bed-and-breakfasting of shares to create losses or reset base cost.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Chargeable Gains

items.stem: An individual sells part of a plot of land. Which formula is used to apportion the original cost between the part sold and the part retained?
options: Cost multiplied by the value retained divided by proceeds
Cost is not apportioned and is deducted in full
Cost multiplied by proceeds divided by proceeds plus the value of the part retained
Cost divided equally between the number of parts
items.explanation: For a part disposal the allowable cost is apportioned using A divided by A plus B, where A is the disposal proceeds and B is the market value of the part retained. This allocates a fair share of the original cost to the part sold.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Chargeable Gains

items.stem: An individual has chargeable gains of 20,000 pounds in the current year and brought-forward allowable capital losses of 5,000 pounds. How is the brought-forward loss relieved?
options: It is set against general income instead of gains
It is lost and cannot be used
It is carried forward again until gains exceed 20,000 pounds
It is set against current-year gains before the annual exempt amount
items.explanation: Brought-forward capital losses are relieved against chargeable gains of the current year before the annual exempt amount is deducted. They may not be set against general income.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Chargeable Gains

items.stem: An individual sells an asset to her adult daughter for 10,000 pounds when its market value is 25,000 pounds. How is the disposal treated for capital gains tax?
options: At market value, because the parties are connected
As exempt, because it is a family transfer
At cost, so no gain arises
At the actual proceeds of 10,000 pounds
items.explanation: A disposal to a connected person is treated as made at market value, so the daughter is treated as acquiring the asset at 25,000 pounds and the seller computes the gain on that value. Family transfers are not exempt in general.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Chargeable Gains

items.stem: An individual gifts a qualifying business asset and both donor and donee elect for hold-over relief. What is the effect of the election?
options: The gain is taxed immediately on the donor
The gain is deferred and reduces the donee's base cost
The gain is exempt for both parties
The gain is carried back to the previous year
items.explanation: Hold-over relief defers the gain so that it is not taxed now but reduces the donee's acquisition cost, meaning it is taxed when the donee later disposes of the asset. It is not an outright exemption.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Chargeable Gains

items.stem: A company has trading profits of 400,000 pounds and a capital loss of 20,000 pounds on the disposal of an investment. How is the capital loss treated?
options: It is added back as a taxable gain
It is deducted from trading profits
It can be set only against capital gains
It is carried forward against future trading profits
items.explanation: Capital losses can be relieved only against capital gains of the same or future periods, never against trading profits. Trading and capital items are kept separate in a corporation tax computation.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Corporation Tax

items.stem: A company makes a trading loss in an accounting period and has other income and gains in that same period. Against what can it relieve the loss on a current-year claim?
options: Against the profits of the previous twelve months only
It cannot be relieved at all
Only against trading profits of the same period
Against total profits of the same period
items.explanation: A current-year trading loss claim relieves the loss against total profits of the same accounting period, including non-trading income and chargeable gains, before deductions such as qualifying gift aid.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Corporation Tax

items.stem: A company makes a trading loss of 100,000 pounds and had taxable trading profits of 60,000 pounds in the preceding twelve months. How much of the loss can it carry back against those earlier profits?
items.explanation: A trading loss can be carried back against the profits of the preceding twelve months, so the relief is limited to the 60,000 pounds of earlier profits. The remaining 40,000 pounds would be carried forward or otherwise relieved.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Corporation Tax

items.stem: A company spends 500,000 pounds on new plant and machinery in its accounting period. Assuming the annual investment allowance is 1,000,000 pounds, how much can the company claim under the allowance?
items.explanation: The annual investment allowance gives 100 percent relief on qualifying plant and machinery up to the limit, so the full 500,000 pounds spent is deductible. The allowance cannot be claimed for more than the amount actually spent.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Corporation Tax

items.stem: A company's main capital allowance pool has a written-down value of 100,000 pounds at the start of the period. Assuming a writing-down allowance of 18 percent, what allowance is available?
items.explanation: The writing-down allowance is 18 percent of the pool's written-down value, so 18 percent of 100,000 pounds is 18,000 pounds. The reduced balance is then carried forward to the next period.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Corporation Tax

items.stem: A company spends 50,000 pounds installing integral features such as a heating and ventilation system in its premises. Into which capital allowance pool does this expenditure fall?
options: The main pool, with a writing-down allowance of 18 percent
The single asset pool at 100 percent
It is not eligible for capital allowances
The special rate pool, with a writing-down allowance of 6 percent
items.explanation: Integral features are allocated to the special rate pool and attract a writing-down allowance of 6 percent. The main pool at 18 percent covers most other plant and machinery.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Corporation Tax

items.stem: A company has one associated company for the whole accounting period. How does this affect the profit limits used to determine the rate of corporation tax?
options: The limits no longer apply at all
items.explanation: The profit limits for the lower and upper rates are divided by the number of associated companies, so one associate halves each limit. This prevents a group from multiplying the benefit of the lower rate.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Corporation Tax

items.stem: A large company has profits above the upper limit and must pay corporation tax by instalments. How are the instalments normally paid?
options: In two equal half-yearly amounts after the year end
In quarterly amounts beginning before the end of the accounting period
In a single payment nine months after the year end
Only when HMRC issues a demand
items.explanation: A large company pays its corporation tax in four quarterly instalments that begin before the end of the accounting period, reflecting that tax is earned over the year. Small companies pay later, nine months and one day after the year end.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Corporation Tax

items.stem: A small company has an accounting period ending on 31 March. When is its corporation tax normally payable?
options: 12 months after the end of the accounting period
9 months and 1 day after the end of the accounting period
On the last day of the accounting period
items.explanation: A small company normally pays its corporation tax nine months and one day after the end of the accounting period. Large companies instead pay by quarterly instalments.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Corporation Tax

items.stem: One company has a trading loss and another company in the same 75 percent group has taxable profits. What relief can be claimed between them?
options: No relief is available between group companies
The loss can be transferred only after a merger
Group relief, by surrendering the loss to the profitable company
items.explanation: Group relief allows a company to surrender its trading loss to another member of the 75 percent group that has taxable profits for the same period. It operates separately from capital gains group relief.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Corporation Tax

items.stem: For the purposes of relief on a disposal of a capital asset from one company to another, what ownership level normally identifies a capital gains group?
items.explanation: Capital gains group relief requires an effective interest of at least 75 percent between the companies, usually through a direct or indirect holding. A 50 or 51 percent holding is not sufficient.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Corporation Tax

items.stem: How are a company's chargeable gains taxed for corporation tax purposes?
options: At a separate capital gains tax rate with its own exemption
As part of total profits, taxed at the corporation tax rate
They are exempt from all tax
items.explanation: A company's chargeable gains are added to its other income and form part of total profits, taxed at the corporation tax rate. Companies do not receive the individual annual exempt amount or the individual capital gains tax rates.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - Corporation Tax

items.stem: A trader's taxable turnover exceeded the VAT registration threshold during June and she must register. By when must she notify HMRC?
options: Within 12 months of the end of June
Within 30 days of the end of June
By 5 April of the following year
items.explanation: A trader whose taxable turnover exceeds the registration threshold must notify HMRC within 30 days of the end of the month in which the threshold was exceeded, so by 30 July here. Registration then takes effect from a set later date.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - VAT and Other Taxes

items.stem: A fully taxable business sells standard-rated goods and buys standard-rated goods for its operations. How does it account for VAT?
options: It reclaims input tax but charges no output tax
It charges output tax but cannot reclaim input tax
It neither charges nor reclaims VAT
It charges output tax on sales and reclaims input tax on purchases
items.explanation: A taxable business charges output tax on its sales and recovers input tax on purchases, paying the difference to HMRC. Only a business making exempt supplies generally cannot recover input tax.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - VAT and Other Taxes

items.stem: A business is on standard quarterly VAT periods. When must it normally submit its VAT return and pay the VAT due?
options: Within one month and seven days after the end of the period
On the last day of the period
Within three months of the end of the period
Only at the end of the tax year
items.explanation: A business on quarterly periods must submit its VAT return and pay the tax within one month and seven days of the period end. The return covers output tax charged less input tax recovered.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - VAT and Other Taxes

items.stem: A business sells goods that are zero-rated for VAT. What is the effect on the VAT it charges and recovers?
options: It must charge the standard rate instead
It charges output tax at 0 percent and can still recover input tax
It charges no output tax and cannot recover input tax
It charges no output tax and recovers only half of its input tax
items.explanation: Zero-rated supplies are taxable supplies on which output tax is charged at 0 percent, so the business can still recover related input tax. Exempt supplies, by contrast, normally block input tax recovery.
items.reference: ACCA TX (UK) Syllabus Study Guide - VAT and Other Taxes
